title: Curved Walls, a Lone Pillar, and Four Posts
subtitle: Finishing the dug-out-pit case, a pillar that almost makes its own walls, and the machloket over four free-standing posts.
sources: Gemara text: Sefaria (William Davidson Edition). Structure and quiz questions 4-6 cross-checked against the Dafyomi Advancement Forum (dafyomi.co.il) quiz for Sukkah 4. Tosfos: dafyomi.co.il's "Point by Point Summary of Tosfos" (Yaakov Montrose, Kollel Iyun Hadaf). The closing point begins a new mishnah clause, continued on 5a.
before: 4a closed with a dug-out pit used to bring a too-short sukkah up to the 10-tefachim minimum, valid only if the gap to the wall is under 3 tefachim. This amud opens by asking why that threshold is 3 tefachim here, but was 4 amos for the platform cases on 4a — same curved-wall idea, different number.

From there: a free-standing pillar that almost creates its own walls by a different principle ("extend and raise the partitions"), and then the real center of the amud — four posts with sechach on top and no walls at all, where Rabbi Yaakov and the Rabbis disagree, and even the Amoraim disagree about what they're disagreeing about.

flow.label: Gemara asks: why 3 tefachim here, but 4 amos for the platform cases?
Answer: two different mechanisms
flow.sub: platform case — a wall already exists, just needs to be "reached" (curved-wall, lenient: 4 amos) · pit case — there's no wall at all yet; only lavud (adjacency) can forge one (strict: 3 tefachim)

flow.label: New case: a lone 10-tefach pillar, big enough on top to be a mini sukkah, standing apart from the walls

items.label: Abaye
items.sub: thought "extend and raise the partitions" makes the pillar's own sides into full walls

items.label: Rava
items.sub: rejects it — a valid sukkah needs conspicuous partitions, and the pillar's sides aren't visible as walls

flow.label: New machloket: four posts, sechach on top, no walls at all
flow.sub: Rabbi Yaakov: fit · the Rabbis: unfit

flow.label: Rav Huna: the machloket is only when the posts sit on a rooftop's edge
flow.sub: over a house's real walls — "extend and raise the partitions" applies there; in the center of the roof, everyone agrees it's unfit

flow.label: Challenged from a beraita about posts driven into open ground
flow.sub: ground is like the center of a roof — yet Rabbi Yaakov still validates it there. Rav Huna's account is refuted (twice) — then partly defended

flow.label: A different beraita: Rabbi Yaakov's own account
flow.sub: a corner-post wide enough to form two 1-tefach "double posts" (deyumdin) counts as two real walls; the Rabbis still require two full walls plus a token third

flow.label: New clause begins
flow.sub: the Mishnah's <10-tefachim rule — the Gemara derives the 10-tefachim measure from the Ark of the Covenant's height — continues on 5a

flowCaption: Two more "is this really a wall" edge-cases, then the machloket over posts with no walls at all.

opinions.claim: A 10-tefachim-tall pillar, wide enough on top to be a minimal sukkah, should be valid via "extend and raise the partitions" — its own four sides, projected upward indefinitely, count as walls.
opinions.basis: Extension of the gud asik mechitzta principle used elsewhere for partitions.

opinions.claim: Rejects it — a sukkah needs conspicuous partitions. The pillar's sides don't visibly project as walls, so the principle doesn't apply here.
opinions.basis: A sukkah-specific requirement of visible partitions, not just any legal fiction of extension.

opinions.claim: Four posts with sechach on top, no walls, can be a valid sukkah — at least on a roof's edge, and per his own account even in the center.
opinions.basis: Beraita; developed via "extend and raise the partitions" and his own deyumdin (double-post) standard.

opinions.claim: Four posts alone are never enough — a valid sukkah needs two complete walls plus a token third wall.
opinions.basis: Beraita; the standard wall-count requirement, unmoved by "extend and raise."

opinions.claim: The Rabbi Yaakov/Rabbis machloket applies only when the four posts sit on the edge of a roof, directly above real walls; in the center of the roof, everyone agrees it's unfit.
opinions.basis: Distinguishes where "extend and raise the partitions" can plausibly apply.

opinions.claim: The machloket is specifically about the center of the roof; possibly it also applies at the edge — left unresolved (teiku).
opinions.basis: A competing read of the same sources Rav Huna was explaining.

script.speaker: 4a's cliffhanger, resolved
script.gloss: If the gap from the dug-out pit's edge to the wall is under 3 tefachim, it's valid — the principle of lavud treats the gap as if it weren't there.

script.speaker: Gemara asks
script.quote: מַאי שְׁנָא הָתָם, דְּאָמְרַתְּ פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא, דְּאָמְרַתְּ פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים?
script.gloss: Why 4 amos for the platform cases, but only 3 tefachim (a much smaller gap) for the pit case?

script.speaker: Gemara answers
script.quote: הָתָם, דְּאִיתֵיהּ לְדוֹפֶן, פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת — סַגִּיא. הָכָא, לְשַׁוּוֹיֵי לְדוֹפֶן, פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים — אִין, אִי לָא — לָא.
script.gloss: In the platform case, a real wall already exists — it just needs to be "reached," and under 4 amos is close enough (curved-wall). In the pit case, there's no wall yet at all — only lavud, the much tighter 3-tefachim adjacency rule, can forge one out of nothing.

script.speaker: New case: the lone pillar
script.quote: הָיְתָה גְּבוֹהָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה, וּבָנָה בָּהּ עַמּוּד שֶׁהוּא גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ הֶכְשֵׁר סוּכָּה — סָבַר אַבָּיֵי לְמֵימַר, גּוּד אַסֵּיק מְחִיצָתָא.
script.gloss: A sukkah over 20 amos with a 10-tefachim pillar built inside it, far from the walls, big enough on top to be a minimal sukkah — Abaye thought to validate it via "extend and raise the partitions": treat the pillar's own sides as walls extending upward indefinitely.

script.speaker: Rava objects
script.gloss: We require conspicuous partitions, and there are none here — the pillar's sides don't actually stick out as visible walls.

script.speaker: New machloket: four posts
script.quote: נָעַץ אַרְבָּעָה קוּנְדֵּיסִין וְסִיכֵּךְ עַל גַּבָּן, רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב מַכְשִׁיר וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹסְלִין.
script.gloss: The Sages taught: one who plants four posts and roofs over them — Rabbi Yaakov deems it fit, the Rabbis deem it unfit.

script.speaker: Rav Huna explains
script.quote: מַחְלוֹקֶת עַל שְׂפַת הַגָּג... אֲבָל בָּאֶמְצַע הַגָּג — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל פְּסוּלָה.
script.gloss: Rav Huna: the machloket is only when the posts are on a rooftop's edge, above the house's real walls — Rabbi Yaakov applies "extend and raise the partitions" there; the Rabbis don't. In the center of the roof, everyone agrees it's unfit.

script.speaker: Rav Nachman's version
script.gloss: Rav Nachman: the machloket is specifically about the center of the roof.

script.speaker: Left unresolved
script.quote: בֵּין בָּזוֹ וּבֵין בָּזוֹ מַחְלוֹקֶת? תֵּיקוּ.
script.gloss: Does Rav Nachman mean the edge case is unanimously valid, or that both edge and center are disputed? No resolution is found — teiku.

script.speaker: A beraita challenges Rav Huna
script.quote: נָעַץ אַרְבָּעָה קוּנְדֵּיסִין בָּאָרֶץ וְסִיכֵּךְ עַל גַּבָּן, רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב מַכְשִׁיר וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹסְלִין.
script.gloss: Another beraita: posts driven into open ground (not a roof) — same machloket, Rabbi Yaakov still validates it.

script.speaker: Refuted
script.quote: וְהָא אֶרֶץ, דִּכְאֶמְצַע הַגָּג דָּמֵי, וְקָא מַכְשִׁיר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב! תְּיוּבְתָּא דְרַב הוּנָא, תְּיוּבְתָּא.
script.gloss: But open ground has no surrounding real walls at all — it's like the center of a roof — and Rabbi Yaakov still validates it there. This refutes Rav Huna's claim that everyone agrees a center-of-roof sukkah is unfit.

script.speaker: A second angle on the same beraita
script.quote: וְעוֹד: בָּאֶמְצַע הוּא דִּפְלִיגִי, אֲבָל עַל שְׂפַת הַגָּג דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרָה!
script.gloss: Furthermore, if the beraita's dispute is about the center, that implies everyone agrees the edge case is valid — a second contradiction of Rav Huna, who held the edge case itself was disputed.

script.speaker: Partly defended
script.quote: פְּלִיגִי בְּאֶמְצַע הַגָּג, וְהוּא הַדִּין עַל שְׂפַת הַגָּג... לְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחוֹ דְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב.
script.gloss: Rav Huna could answer: they may well dispute the edge case too — the beraita picked the harder, center-of-roof case specifically to show how far Rabbi Yaakov's leniency extends.

script.speaker: Rabbi Yaakov's own standard
script.quote: רוֹאִין כׇּל שֶׁאִילּוּ יֵחָקְקוּ וְיֵחָלְקוּ, וְיֵשׁ בָּהֶן טֶפַח לְכָאן וְטֶפַח לְכָאן — נִידּוֹנִין מִשּׁוּם דְּיוֹמָד... וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ שְׁתַּיִם כְּהִלְכָתָן, וּשְׁלִישִׁית אֲפִילּוּ טֶפַח.
script.gloss: A further beraita: Rabbi Yaakov — if a corner post, notionally split, would give a tefach's width on each of its two faces, that counts as a "double post" (deyumad) — effectively two walls. The Rabbis require two complete, standard walls plus a third of even just a tefach (a halachah transmitted from Sinai).

script.speaker: New clause begins
script.gloss: The mishnah's next clause: a sukkah under 10 tefachim is unfit. From where is this measure derived? The Gemara traces it to the height of the Ark of the Covenant in the Mishkan — continued on 5a.

tosfos.summary: Rashi and Tosfos disagree on whether a partial wall combines with a ditch to form a full halachic wall, comparing Sukkah to Shabbos domains.

points.label: (a)-(b) Opinion & Question
points.he: מכאן קשיא לפי מה שפי׳ בקונט׳ בריש פרק שני דגיטין... הא אשכחן הכא לענין סוכה דמצטרפין
points.en: Rashi (Gittin 15b) holds a 5-tefach ditch plus a 5-tefach wall above it do NOT combine into one 10-tefach wall for Shabbos domains — but our Gemara clearly treats the parallel combination as valid for sukkah. Why the difference?

points.label: (c)-(f) More questions
points.he: וכן בפ״ק דשבת... ועוד מקשה רבינו תם... ועוד אמרינן בסוף פרק כל גגות
points.en: Several more Shabbos-law sources seem to support combining a shallow pit with a short wall above it into a full 10-tefach partition — in tension with Rashi's Gittin ruling.

points.label: (g) Opinion #2
points.he: אלא יש לומר דגידוד חמשה ומחיצה חמשה לענין שתי חצירות זו למעלה מזו איירי
points.en: Those Shabbos sources are really about two stacked courtyards, not a general combination rule — so they don't actually contradict Rashi.

points.label: (k) Answer
points.he: ויש לומר דלא דמי רשות שבת שהוא למנוע רגל רבים לסוכה דבעינן מחיצות סמוכות לסכך
points.en: A Shabbos private-domain wall only needs to keep the public from walking through — a looser standard. Sukkah requires walls actually adjacent to the sechach, a stricter one. That's why the two areas of law don't need to match.

tosfos.summary: Why a later case (roofing over a beam-less porch) still counts as having noticeable walls, unlike Abaye's rejected pillar.

points.label: (a) Observation
points.en: The Gemara concludes we require conspicuous partitions.

points.label: (b) Implied Question
points.he: ולא דמי לסיכך על גבי אכסדרה שאין לה פצימין דשילהי פירקין (דף יח:)
points.en: Unlike the later case (18b) of roofing over a porch with no side-beams — why is that one still valid?

points.label: (c) Answer
points.he: דפי תקרה חשיב שפיר מחיצות הניכרות
points.en: Because the edge of the roof there is itself considered a conspicuous wall.

tosfos.summary: Why posts on a roof's edge, above real walls, count as more "noticeable" than a lone pillar.

points.label: (a) Explanation
points.he: דחשיב מחיצות ניכרות טפי מעמוד משום דניכרות בבית
points.en: Posts at a roof's edge are recognized as more of a wall than a lone pillar, because they read as an extension of the house's actual walls.

tosfos.summary: Why Sukkah's double-post standard (a tefach) is more lenient than the parallel rule for well-partitions on Shabbos (a full amah).

points.label: (a) Implied Question
points.he: והא דבעינן אמה גבי פסי ביראות פרק עושין פסין (עירובין דף יז:)
points.en: For pasei biraot (well-partitions on Shabbos), each side needs a full amah — why does sukkah settle for just a tefach?

points.label: (b) Answer
points.en: The laws of Shabbos partitions were made more stringent.

tosfos.summary: This sugya is the actual source for the 10-tefachim wall requirement used throughout the laws of Shabbos.

points.label: (a) Observation
points.he: והא דבעינן נמי גבי שבת מחיצה עשרה מהכא ילפינן
points.en: The requirement that a Shabbos partition be 10 tefachim tall is itself derived from here.
